Its root is the final entitlement record, with the two earlier quantities initially unrecorded. Each is a nonfinancial database_service_record, grounded in database_evt_category_meters. Task 1 retains primary database billing review and correction, with customer-owned authorization and a four-write workflow. The categories and customer identifiers remain disjoint from other difficulties.

Interpretation checkpoint: the unique workflow will orchestrate the entire second consultation; the root problem is its terminal extended policy, and the dependency graph refers to the distinct atomic problems included in that workflow. This preserves exact full GT/workflow step alignment without making a workflow depend on a write that it itself includes. Independent policy audit must assess this interpretation.

Task 0 design thesis: a customer asks to correct the database retention entitlement shown for one contract and billing month. The policy requires external backup coverage reconciliation before native retention allocation, and native allocation before the consolidated entitlement can be registered. The customer names none of those prerequisites. Eight authoritative retained-storage export segments, existing reversed/rejected evidence, database tier capacities, retained days and active Managed Backup capacity determine each quantity. The writes are nonfinancial service entitlements, not fabricated payment or approval events. Root target is a corrected entitlement, not a customer-supplied number.

Scope reservation: task 0 uses retained backup-storage entitlements; task 1 uses primary node billing correction and its signed claim. Base automatic billing obligations must be excluded by seed having existing financial source charges rather than leaving unbilled measured services.

Task 1 scope claim: the occupied retained-storage allocation chain is excluded. The second consultation concerns an erroneous primary node invoice. Its separate primary-export reconciliation calculates per-node usage, an accountant corrects the invoice target, the customer signs the exact correction authorization, and the agent books the negative invoice adjustment. The independent cross-category numeric evidence is the resource_count of a singly matched active Managed Backup contract in the same billing entity: the signed linked topology uses that node count, and provider exports and source invoice must carry the same count. It never grants free primary usage or a backup price discount. Dividing aggregate node-hours by that authoritative count yields the per-node evidence; multiplying it by the count in the review restores the correct primary service quantity. The authorization and credit select only the original charge whose resource count agrees with that same topology. Prior corrections and rejected exports are reconciled; no cash refund is implicit.

Task 1 root is the final invoice correction policy. The graph includes the distinct average-usage problem, corrected-target review problem and customer authorization problem, with three explicit prerequisite edges. One workflow orchestrates all four atomic writes and exactly matches all four gold tools, owners and order. Initial raw exports and commercial approval are official and preexisting; each computational assessment and signature is synchronous in this environment. No physical service event, bank clearing or external approval is manufactured.

Task 1 policy checkpoint: four independent primary correction policies and the single four-step workflow persisted. Base prices are preserved: backup topology is a physical resource-count input, never a discount. The primary average is per-node; the review multiplies by the same count before applying the database negotiated/standard rate, configuration and region. All constants in params reproduce base region_factors without overriding their values. Remaining overcharge excludes service credits, and the final credit is signed negative. A customer signature is required by the declared signed correction route and cannot be written by the agent.

Capability cards before tools: primary_average (agent) updates the existing per-node assessment quantity and completes it; primary_target (agent accountant) updates the existing review corrected net/tax and records its authoritative incorrect decision; correction_consent (user) creates a personally signed correction request with pending status and exact authorized USD amount; primary_correction (agent) creates one negative receivable credit linked to original charge, approved review and request. Every receipt contains identifiers, computed numeric value and successful status. The tools make one update/create each and do not read, validate or aggregate evidence.

## Source audit rework round 2

Read every audit file in full: 0.md, 0_independent_execution_frozen.json, 1.md, 1_independent_execution_frozen.json, _difficulty.md, blind_freeze_manifest.json, charter_counterexamples.json, reveal_log.txt. The sole defect input is this audit directory. Task 0 and both actual-world replays were independently PASS; changes will preserve those results. P1/P2/P3 are extended-domain defects, not frozen-base defects; none is proposed as BLUEPRINT-KNOWN.

P1 — OPEN -> corrected scope persisted. The signed credit-only route previously admitted undercharges. All four primary policies now explicitly require a strictly positive remaining overcharge after cumulative correction adjustments, determined from source evidence and the reconstructed target before selecting the route. Undercharges remain governed by the inherited positive-debit clause, equality by the inherited no-write clause; this workflow does not claim either branch. The broad differing-target sentence is removed. The P1 witness2000 versus2433.60 is therefore outside this workflow and still calls for the inherited433.60 debit. Task1 is inside:4200-100>2433.60.

P2 — corrected aggregate recovery persisted. The per-node assessment remains a real required value-input write. Before billing, target reconstructs original archive hundredths from its completed six-place value. For Q=k/100 and n<=64, average rounding error times n is at most32 millionths, strictly less than half a hundredth (5000 millionths), so rounding reconstructed aggregate to a hundredth returns Q exactly. P2 witness: average3333 millionths times3=9999 millionths; (9999+5000)//10000=1 hundredth, then .01*.5 rounds to.01 as base requires. Added pricing, category-meter, tax and correction references to target computation lineage; no base clause or parameter is overridden. Current target remains2433.60; omission of the average still yields aggregate0 and target0. Exact integer-ratio averaging also preserves ties without changing displayed precision.

P3 — integer money arithmetic persisted. Target converts its permitted <=standard six-decimal rate to integer millionths, two-decimal configuration/region factors to integer hundredths, then multiplies integers only. Half-up cents uses (integer trillionths+5000000000)//10000000000. P3 witness numerator=35000000000 and resulting cents4, yielding.04, so no binary product precedes the tie decision. Earlier statements claiming that arbitrary float product plus0.5 solved all ties are explicitly withdrawn; this integer numerator replaces that method for the affected monetary target. Current values remain unchanged; domain witness verification follows.

O1 — CLOSED: added literal requires_external_wait:false and zero_wait_proof to the workflow and every step, with source-kind lists and concrete explanations matching the already-passing task contracts. No full UUID generation transcript was retained; final names alone cannot independently prove random origin. This is an evidentiary observation, not a demonstrated policy/task defect; preserve the seven unique unpatterned names rather than inventing retrospective provenance.
